title: A clear boundary and ambiguous image
meaning: Your shared view can clearly distinguish observation from imagination while the image itself still feels ambiguous.
text: You can understand an image’s boundary while its ambiguity remains. The Hermit in the physical position of Ajna suggests considering impressions and sharing understanding. The Moon in energy supports wanting to clarify the boundary between observation and imagination. The Moon in emotions experiences a continuing image’s many meanings. Her first role concerns wanting to distinguish layers; her second concerns feeling an impression’s instability. Both may understand which detail produced an association while the image still changes and resists one name. Your shared view holds both layers.

Suppose you examine a houseplant’s shadow on a wall. After reflection, one person explains how overlapping leaves suggest a face. **A clear boundary need not make the image itself unambiguous.** Both see where the impression came from. Yet the shadow keeps looking alternately like a profile and a bird’s outline. You can name observable lines while preserving changing associations. Shared understanding chooses no single image: it shows what relates to leaf shapes and what arises through reading them imaginatively. The response remains fluid.

The risk is trying to end that fluidity through explaining every association afresh. Distinguishing layers becomes an endless examination of impressions. Wanting a clear boundary preserves proportion: the cause is understood while the image can freely change its shades without needing a final definition.
